title: intersectional-slo-holdoff-and-atomic-circuit-sequencer
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces an SLO holdoff matrix that reduces oscillations during cross-region soft-failovers.
Adds an atomic circuit sequencer to serialize circuit state transitions and prevent race-induced reopen storms.
Improves telemetry for circuit transitions and pre-failover throttles to help postmortems and alert tuning.
description: Context: We observed repeated reopen/reclose oscillation during multi-tenant regional pressure events. Root cause analysis pointed to interleaved circuit transitions and simultaneous tenant-level SLO relaxations that caused cascading reassignment of requests and KV-drain churn. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) an intersectional SLO holdoff matrix that enforces a short, configurable holdoff when multiple SLO signals converge for the same tenant/route, preventing aggressive successive concessions; (2) an atomic circuit sequencer in the control plane that ensures circuit state transitions (open -> probing -> closed) for a given region/zone are applied serially with a bounded window to prevent flip-flop storms. The changes are intentionally conservative and feature-flagged behind `slo_holdoff_v2` and `atomic_circuit_sequencer`. Checklist: - [x] Implement holdoff matrix and config knobs - [x] Add sequencer store and transition API - [x] Wire flags and defaults for staged rollout - [x] Add unit + integration tests for concurrency cases - [x] Add e2e runbook snippet and dashboard tiles Description of changes (commits summary): - feat(slo): add holdoff_matrix service and evaluation logic; default holdoff 12s for intersection cases - feat(controlplane): atomic sequencer service with in-memory fast-path and durable index fallback - fix(kv): ensure kv-drain tasks read sequencer lease to avoid overlapping evacuations - test: add race condition tests that previously reproduced flip-flop - docs: runbook update + observability dashboard additions Files changed (high level): - src/controlplane/slo/holdoff_manager.go: new evaluation rules, configuration parsing, metric hooks - src/controlplane/sequencer/sequencer.go: sequencer state machine, lease management, persistence interface - src/serving/circuit/circuit_controller.rs: consume sequencer API for transition requests - src/serving/kv/drain_worker.py: check sequencer lease before starting cross-region evacuations - tests/unit/slo/holdoff_test.go: deterministic unit tests for intersection cases - tests/integration/sequencer_race_test.go: concurrent transition simulation - docs/runbooks/oscillation-mitigation.md: runbook and rollout steps Review conversation: - Miguel Torres (review): "Important direction; major concern is ensuring the sequencer failure modes don't silently block legitimate reopen when a node is slow. Can we tighten the fallback to a soft timeout and telemetry?" - Aisha Patel (author): "Agree. Sequencer has a default lease of 30s and an observable TTL expiry counter. I added a soft-timeout path that will escalate a transition if the sequencer lease isn't renewed and includes an audit counter so it surfaces in alerts." - Priya Shah (review): "Tests look good. Please add a small e2e that runs against the staging control plane with flags enabled for 5m to ensure no deadlocks." - Aisha Patel: "Added a teardown-safe e2e script (tests/e2e/sequencer_smoke.sh) and ran it on staging; results are linked below." - Ethan Liu (approval): "Approve after squashing; watch the metric slo.holdoff.count for high values during rollout." CI check summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass (integration suite had one transient timeout earlier, rerun successful) - lint: pass - security-scan: pass (no new findings) Observability & rollout: - Feature flags: slo_holdoff_v2 (off by default), atomic_circuit_sequencer (gradual rollout) - Recommended rollout plan: canary (5% regions) -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with heartbeat TTL monitoring - Dashboards added: slo.holdoff.count, sequencer.leases.active, sequencer.lease_expiry.rate - Alerts added: sequencer.lease_expiry.rate > 1/min for 5m, slo.holdoff.count spike > 10x baseline for 15m Backwards compatibility & safety: - Telemetry-only guardrails enabled initially: flag to run in "observe" mode where holdoff decisions are logged but not enforced. - Sequencer uses an in-memory fast-path for low-latency transitions and falls back to control-plane durable index if leadership is ambiguous. This avoids adding a synchronous control-plane hop on every transition in the common case. Migration notes: - Customers using private deployments: control plane library bump required (v1.12.0) and operator action to enable feature gates. - For Dedicated: config knobs exposed via console under "SLO enforcement". Merge details: merged via squash-merge by Priya Shah. Merge SHA: 7b3e4b9f8a2c3d5e6f0192a4c5b6d7e8f9a0b1c2 Post-merge follow-ups (todo): - Monitor for any sequencer-induced stalls and add a metric-driven auto-disable if the sequencer blocks > 1% of transitions for > 10m. - Add long-tail test to perf-lab to validate latencies with sequencer fast-path. Related: ENG-4298 (oscillation postmortem), SUP-1184 (customer incident for region flip-flop). Links: - Staging e2e run: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/12345 - Postmortem: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4298/oscillation-analysis
